correctness.rationale: The homogeneous recurrence makes the increment sign equivalent to a scalar level crossing for g(x)=x(1-x^2). The exact starter is strictly increasing, and the unimodality of g gives one and only one crossing on its decreasing branch. Substitution into the exact Allen-Cahn flow yields the stated closed-form threshold; differentiation proves transversality. The alpha>1 extension is the same argument with level q g(a). A standalone numerical artifact checks the formulas and sign changes for representative parameters.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 source proves stabilized CN/AB reversal using a conservative sufficient step-size bound and then transfers the strict decrement to small nonhomogeneous perturbations. It does not state the exact if-and-only-if onset, closed-form threshold state, exact gap, transversality, or general over-extrapolation threshold law. Earlier inspected stabilized-CN/AB and Allen-Cahn ODE-stability work addresses energy/error estimates or different schemes. Searches found no inspected prior coverage of the formulas. Originality is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result supplies a sharp failure certificate for a widely used stabilized second-order phase-field integrator: it identifies precisely when the first post-starter pointwise direction reverses, shows stabilization cannot move that onset in the homogeneous test, strengthens the perturbative active-diffusion failure regime to the exact boundary, and isolates over-extrapolation as the mechanism.
